# Running the Pipeline

## Launch

```bash
sbatch MicroCPipe.sh
```

`MicroCPipe.sh` follows the dietJuicer launcher pattern: it sources the
site's `profiles/<site>/env.sh` (software setup), builds a venv in `env/`
from `config/requirements.txt` (without activating it, so it never shadows the conda
environments' own Python), and runs Snakemake with that site's profile
(`hpcProfile` in the config, or `$MICROC_PROFILE`, or `--profile`). On
`profiles/local`, run it with `bash` instead of `sbatch`. Each rule becomes
its own SLURM job.

## What happens

```text
align (per sequencing run) ─► dedup (per group) ─► split ─┬─► cool ─► mcool
                                                          ├─► hic
                                                          └─► sort_bam ─► library_complexity
dedup stats ─► qc_summary
all of the above ─► benchmark_summary, qc_report
```

| Rule | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `align` | `bwa mem -5SP -T0` -> `pairtools parse` -> `pairtools sort`, one job per samplesheet row |
| `dedup` | Merges a group's runs, marks duplicates, writes the stats |
| `split` | `.pairs.gz` (only unique UU/UR/RU pairs, via `pairtools select`) and an unsorted BAM |
| `sort_bam` | Sorted, indexed BAM (when `make_bam` is on) |
| `qc_summary` | Dovetail-style QC table |
| `library_complexity` | `preseq lc_extrap` (non-fatal: on a very shallow library it writes a header-only table and the dashboard shows no curve) |
| `cool` / `mcool` / `hic` | The contact maps |
| `analysis_*` | Optional cooltools / mustache |
| `benchmark_summary` | Runtime / memory table |
| `qc_report` | The static dashboard |

Resources for each rule are in `profiles/<site>/config.yaml` under
`set-threads:` and `set-resources:`.

## Dry run first

```bash
bash MicroCPipe.sh -n
```

Prints every job and shell command that would be submitted; nothing runs.
Use it after every change to the samplesheet or config: it shows which
groups Snakemake found, how many alignment jobs there are, and which files
are missing. Extra arguments go straight to `snakemake`, e.g.
`bash MicroCPipe.sh --conda-create-envs-only` builds the environments
without running anything.

## The Merge workflow

After the Core workflow has finished, combine libraries (for example
technical replicates) into one deeper map:

1. List each library's `.pairs.gz` in `MicroCMergeSamplesheet.txt`, with the
   metadata columns of `merge: mergeBy:`.
2. Check it:

    ```bash
    bash MicroCMerge.sh -n
    ```

3. Run it:

    ```bash
    sbatch MicroCMerge.sh
    ```

For each merged group it writes `{group}_merged.pairs.gz` (with `{group}` = `merged_<...>`) and then the
formats listed in `outputs` (`.cool`, `.mcool`, `.hic`, and any `analysis`)
into `output/{group}/`. Merge groups are named `merged_<mergeBy values>`, e.g.
`output/merged_Example_GM12878_1/merged_Example_GM12878_1.mcool`, so they never
collide with Core outputs. The merge uses the same config, profile and
`outputDir` as the Core workflow. It makes no QC dashboard: the QC of a
merged map is the QC of the libraries that went into it.

## Email notifications

Set an address and the workflow emails you once when it starts, once when it
finishes, and once if any job fails (not once per job):

```bash
export MICROC_EMAIL=<your-email>   # e.g. in ~/.bashrc
```

The address can also go in `notify: email:` in the config; the environment
variable keeps it out of a shared repo and wins if both are set. With
neither set, nothing is sent. `notify: events:` picks which of `start`,
`success`, `error` to send, and `notify: command:` is the shell command that
sends one message (default `mail -s {subject} {email}`, with the body on
stdin; use e.g. `sendmail {email}` on clusters without `mail`, putting a
`Subject:` line in the body). The failure email includes the last 40 lines
of the Snakemake log. Dry runs (`-n`) send nothing, and a failed email never
fails the workflow. Check your cluster can send mail with
`echo test | mail -s test $MICROC_EMAIL`.

The launcher job itself also carries `#SBATCH --mail-type=END,FAIL,TIME_LIMIT_80`;
`sbatch --mail-user=$MICROC_EMAIL MicroCPipe.sh` directs SLURM's own mail.

## Using a different config

```bash
sbatch MicroCPipe.sh --configfile config/my_run.yaml
```

The file must be a complete config. Keep one config per project to avoid
editing the shipped one.

## After a failed run

```bash
bash unlock.sh               # release the Snakemake lock
sbatch MicroCPipe.sh         # --rerun-incomplete is on by default
```

For the Merge workflow use `bash unlock.sh --merge`. If you used another
config or profile, pass the same `--configfile` and `--profile` to
`unlock.sh`.

## Resuming and re-running

Snakemake decides what to run from which output files exist, so resuming is
the same as launching again:

- **Resume after a crash or time-out.** Run `unlock.sh` if the lock error
  appears, then launch again. Finished jobs are kept; failed ones are rerun
  (`--rerun-incomplete` is on, and `--keep-going` lets independent groups
  finish when one fails).
- **Add a library.** Add rows to the samplesheet and launch again; groups
  that are already finished are not touched. Adding a row to an existing
  group changes that group, so it is realigned and redone from `dedup` on.
- **Change one parameter.** A parameter that is part of a rule (for
  example `resolutions`) makes Snakemake rerun the affected rules.
  Check what it plans with a dry run first.
- **Rebuild just the dashboard.** The dashboard step does not notice edits
  to `qc_thresholds`, so force it:

    ```bash
    bash MicroCPipe.sh --forcerun qc_report
    ```

- **Stop part-way.** `--until <rule>` stops after a rule, e.g.
  `bash MicroCPipe.sh --until dedup`.

## Monitoring

| Log | Path |
|-----|------|
| Launcher (main Snakemake process) | `MicroCPipe-{jobid}.out` |
| Each job's log | `output/{group}/logs/{group}_{rule}.log` (alignment: `{run}_align.log`) |
| Dashboard log | `output/qc/qc_report.log` |
| SLURM job logs | `output/logs_slurm/` |
| Per-job run time and memory | `output/{group}/benchmarks/`, and `output/benchmarking.tsv` once the run ends |

```bash
squeue -u $USER                                              # waiting (PD) and running (R) jobs
sacct -u $USER -S today --format=JobID,JobName%25,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS   # finished jobs, with peak memory
```

`State` values to know: `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` (read the job's log),
`OUT_OF_MEMORY` (raise `mem_mb`), `TIMEOUT` (raise `runtime`). More in
[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).

## Output structure

Everything is written under `outputDir`: `output/` in the folder you launch
from by default, or under `$MICROC_OUTPUT_ROOT` when that is set.

```text
output/
├── benchmarking.tsv
├── qc/
│   ├── MicroC_qc_report.html
│   └── qc_report.log
├── {group}/
│   ├── {group}.pairs.gz              # Core (unique pairs only); Merge: merged_<g>/merged_<g>_merged.pairs.gz
│   ├── {group}.cool
│   ├── {group}.mcool
│   ├── {group}.hic
│   ├── {group}_dedup_stats.txt
│   ├── {group}_qc_summary.txt
│   ├── {group}_libraryComplexity.txt
│   ├── {group}_mapped.PT.bam(.bai)
│   ├── analysis/
│   ├── logs/
│   └── benchmarks/
└── logs_slurm/
```

## Troubleshooting

A longer symptom -> cause -> fix table is in [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).
The short version:

| Symptom | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Snakemake lock error | `bash unlock.sh` then resubmit |
| `hic` job killed or Java heap error | Raise `hic: mem_mb` in the profile (the heap is 85% of it unless `javaMem` is set) ([Recipes](recipes.qmd#when-the-hic-step-runs-out-of-memory)) |
| A rule ends in `TIMEOUT` | Raise that rule's `runtime:` in `profiles/<site>/config.yaml`, `bash unlock.sh`, resubmit |
| `MissingInputException` | A FASTQ or `pairs` path does not exist from where you launched |
| Output in the launch folder instead of scratch | `MICROC_OUTPUT_ROOT` not set in the shell that ran `sbatch`; `source ~/.bashrc` and resubmit |
| Jobs on the wrong cluster's partitions or account | `MICROC_PROFILE` not set; `echo $MICROC_PROFILE`, or pass `--profile` |
| No emails arrive | Test `echo test \| mail -s test $MICROC_EMAIL`; change `notify: command:` |
| A job failed | Read its log in `output/{group}/logs/` |
